findings.statement: a mapped index opens at least 10x faster than a decoded one
a mapped index costs less than half the bytes per key of a decoded one
findings.detail: decoded 226 B/key resident against a mapped section of 99 B/key. Measured against the section rather than against resident size, because a read pass faults in block and cache pages common to both arms and dilutes the difference: on that measure it reads 168 B/key. The mapped arm's pages are also file-backed, so N readers share one copy where the decoded arm pays N times

findings.statement: point reads do not get slower
a checkpoint does not cost more than 16 bytes per key of permanent file growth
findings.detail: heap 0.0 B/key per checkpoint, flat 0.0 B/key. Sections are reclaimed once no reader can reach them, so a long-running store reaches steady state instead of growing without bound in checkpoint count. Before that fix this was 9.2 and 66.9 B/key respectively, forever -- a pre-existing leak the flat format made expensive enough to notice (0.0x)

findings.statement: the file grows by less than 10% in exchange
findings.detail: at one checkpoint, heap 559.8 MB -> flat 1013.4 MB (+81.0%). An index read in place cannot be compressed, and compactness is one of the two axes this engine wins on. Measured on the minimal file: after six checkpoints the same stores are 660.7 and 1015.8 MB, but that gap is holes left by reclaimed sections rather than the price of the format
